name: presenter-startup
description: Presenter/window-jump regression (0851a03) plus the theme/resize/Cmd+Q class. Launches on a FOREIGN-profile, UNTHEMED startup space, switches to a THEMED cross-profile space, and asserts one window survives, the backdrop actually changed, resize still works, and Cmd+Q quits. Two traps would make it measure nothing: Cmd+2 is not the space-switch chord (that is Cmd+Shift+Arrow), so the space never switches and theme_changed compares two byte-identical frames, and without `activate` the chord goes to Finder on a clean snapshot. The switch is gated on the target space's tab URL appearing, the same proof a sibling scenario uses, so this cannot silently go back to measuring a switch that did not happen. The chord itself is gone now too: kNextSpace (chrome/browser/ui/atrium/atrium_native_hotkey_map.mm) still returns false, a gap other scenarios hit too, so Cmd+Shift+Right never lands the switch it is asked for. The switch now clicks the sidebar's own space dot instead - `.spacedots .sdot[data-space-index]`, the exact route routing-moves-the-tab.json and a settingsSpaceOpened pick both use - which calls BrowserController::SelectSpace directly and never touches the broken hotkey map. An extra assertion reads SelectSpace's own log line so a vacuous tab-url match can no longer be the only proof the switch happened.

actions.note: let the foreign/unthemed startup space finish rendering

ssh-launched Atrium is not frontmost on a clean snapshot, so without this the Cmd+2 below lands in Finder and the space never switches - the same note every other scenario in this directory carries. Its absence here is why theme_changed compared two identical frames.
let the window come forward before the switch
backdrop on the unthemed startup space

actions.expression: (() => { const dot = document.querySelector('.spacedots .sdot[data-space-index="1"]'); if (!dot) return 'no-dot'; dot.click(); return 'clicked'; })()
actions.note: switch to the next space - the THEMED cross-profile one. Cmd+Shift+Arrow's kNextSpace still returns false, so this clicks the sidebar's own space dot instead, the same BrowserController::SelectSpace route routing-moves-the-tab.json and a settingsSpaceOpened pick both use.

wait for the SWITCH to actually land rather than sleeping a fixed time: example.com is space 2's tab, example.org space 1's. The URL is logged on navigation start, so it fires even though the VM has no internet and the page never loads.
let the cross-profile swap and the theme animation settle after the switch has been confirmed

assertions.desc: the sidebar's own dot for the themed space was there to click

assertions.label: space-switched
assertions.note: Proves the space switch happened before anything below is worth reading. Without it theme_changed reports UNCHANGED for two different reasons - the theme regressed, or the switch never ran - and cannot tell you which. That ambiguity is what this scenario sat in.

assertions.label: space-switch-confirmed-by-controller
assertions.note: the dot click's own proof, independent of the tab-url gate above: BrowserController::SelectSpace names both ends of the move, so a vacuous tab-url match can no longer be the only evidence the switch happened.

assertions.desc: exactly ONE real Atrium window across the switch (a second ordered NSWindow is the presenter/jump regression)

themed backdrop actually changed (raw-pixel region compare, not a VLOG). Region is in frame PIXEL space (2x retina) over the sidebar margin - tune against a real before frame if it overlaps opaque web content

window still responds to an AX resize after the switch. the target was 1200x800, which the probe VM's 1024x768 display cannot accommodate - the window was clamped to the screen and the assertion had been red since at least 2026-07-27 for a reason that had nothing to do with Atrium. 900x600 fits with room to spare.
